environment.baselineFailure: Workspace Vault public API must exist

prompt:
Deliver Workspace Vault, a complete offline backup and recovery product for local development workspaces, as a standalone package in contrib/workspace-vault of this real fs-extra repository. The user needs versioned backups before project migrations, portable archives, crash recovery, and a local job dashboard. Preserve the parent project's existing behavior, dependencies, package manifest and original tests. This is one coherent release: complete the implementation, maintained tests, documentation, packaging and operational checks autonomously. Organize your own milestones and keep a durable project work log; do not stop after a scaffold or an intermediate milestone. No timing targets or intentional delays are part of the product.

Public package contract: Node >=22; CommonJS index.js and ESM index.mjs export the same createVault and createServer functions by identity. await createVault(storePath) initializes or opens a store and returns the asynchronous API below. Keep the standalone package installable outside this checkout without any runtime dependencies. Its package.json declares name workspace-vault, version 1.0.0, conditional import/require exports, and a workspace-vault executable at bin/workspace-vault.js. Relative public path arguments resolve from process.cwd(). Errors use codes ERR_VAULT_INVALID (invalid input or unsafe paths), ERR_VAULT_CORRUPT (invalid stored/bundle bytes), ERR_VAULT_CONFLICT (incompatible live state), ERR_VAULT_NOT_FOUND, and ERR_VAULT_BUSY as appropriate. Cooperative AbortSignal rejection preserves signal.reason exactly. Reject invalid options explicitly, clean owned temporary resources, and avoid unhandled rejections.

1. Content-addressed storage. snapshot(sourceDirectory, options={label,exclude,signal,onProgress}) returns a version:1 manifest {version,id,entries,label,createdAt}. Entries are sorted by portable relative path using byte ordering, include empty directories, omit the root itself, and are deterministic. An entry is {path,type:'file',mode,size,hash}, {path,type:'directory',mode}, or {path,type:'symlink',target}; mode is permission bits 0..511, size is bytes, hash lowercase SHA-256. Canonical entry property order is exactly as shown; id is SHA-256 of UTF-8 JSON.stringify(entries), so identical content and permissions have the same id across roots, labels and times. Preserve relative and dangling symlinks without traversing them, binary bytes, Unicode/newline/quote names and executable modes. exclude is an array of exact portable relative path prefixes (a excludes a and a/..., not abc), applied to directories before traversal. Never write into source. Reject root overlap with the store using real paths, including symlink aliases; reject unsupported entry types and escaping manifest paths. Stream file hashing/storage; stable memory use must not depend on total tree size. Detect files changing during capture and fail without publishing a partial manifest. Store raw blobs at objects/<sha256>, manifests at manifests/<id>.json, and maintain an atomic durable index. Repeated snapshots deduplicate blobs. listSnapshots() returns manifest summaries containing id,label,createdAt in deterministic order; getSnapshot(id) validates and returns its manifest. A repeated id is one snapshot, with the latest supplied label.

2. Restore and comparison. restore(snapshotId,destination,options={mirror,conflict,dryRun,journalPath,signal,onProgress}) defaults to mirror:false and conflict:'overwrite'. It returns {snapshotId,status:'completed'|'planned',operations,completedOperations,totalOperations}. Operations expose path and action ('mkdir','copy','symlink','remove') in deterministic dependency order. dryRun:true returns status planned, zero completed operations, and performs no destination or journal mutation. Equal bytes, modes and link text are no-ops; preserve their mtimes. Preserve destination extras unless mirror:true. Support file/directory/link replacements. conflict:'error' rejects changed existing entries before any destination mutation; conflict:'skip' preserves conflicting existing entries while restoring other safe paths (skip conflicting subtrees). Validate ALL required objects and manifest paths before the first destination mutation. Reject an overlapping store/destination and symlink ancestors redirecting writes outside the destination; never modify outside it. diff(fromId,toId) returns sorted path arrays {added,removed,modified} including metadata or link-target changes. verify(snapshotId?) returns {ok,checkedObjects,errors}; every error includes code and the affected hash or path. Missing or corrupt objects are reported, not silently repaired; corruption must prevent restore preflight with ERR_VAULT_CORRUPT.

3. Durable recovery. journalPath is optional, absolute, outside store and destination. A journal records version:1, snapshotId, canonical destination, status:'running'|'completed', completed (operation indexes), the fixed plan and enough original/result preconditions to resume. Journal files and their direct parent cannot be symlinks. Do not overwrite unrelated existing journal data. Atomic file replacement and fsync of relevant file/directory/journal state must commit before progress. onProgress({snapshotId,operationIndex,operation,completedOperations,totalOperations}) is awaited once for each newly committed operation. Thrown callback errors propagate unchanged; later operations do not start. Cancellation while a callback is pending must settle promptly without later filesystem writes or unhandled late rejection. Abort before work must have no filesystem effects. Reopening the store in another process and restoring with the same journal resumes after real SIGKILL at a committed progress boundary. A completed journal is an idempotent no-op, with no repeated progress or mtime change. External changes to already committed outputs reject ERR_VAULT_CONFLICT. Document the exact crash boundary, fsync/platform limits and partial-result semantics; whole-tree atomicity is not promised.

4. Portable streaming bundles. exportSnapshot(id,bundlePath,options={signal}) atomically writes an NDJSON bundle outside the store. First line is {type:'header',format:'workspace-vault',version:1,snapshot:<manifest>}. Then chunk records {type:'chunk',hash,offset,data}, data canonical base64 of at most 65536 decoded bytes, monotonic contiguous offsets per object, each unique referenced object included once. Final line is {type:'end'}. importSnapshot(bundlePath,options={signal}) validates structure, safe paths, canonical manifest id, chunk offsets, strict base64, all sizes and hashes, missing/extra objects, supported version, end marker and trailing records before publishing; returns the imported manifest. Stage untrusted data outside published objects/index and clean owned staging on failure/cancel. Failed import must leave a pre-existing vault's logical state and referenced objects unchanged. Export/import round-trips across store locations and handles zero-byte files, duplicates, multi-chunk binary files and Unicode. Reject truncation, corruption, traversal and unsupported versions with ERR_VAULT_CORRUPT or ERR_VAULT_INVALID. Never trust source absolute roots from imported data.

5. Retention and process concurrency. prune({keep:[snapshotIds],dryRun:false}) validates all kept ids then returns sorted {removedSnapshots,removedObjects}; remove only unreachable blobs after safely publishing the retained index. dryRun is entirely read-only. Concurrent snapshots from independent processes cannot lose index entries or expose partial objects. Coordinate store mutations and restores with bounded locks; active lock contention returns ERR_VAULT_BUSY or waits for at most a documented bound. Recover abandoned ownership after process death using verified local process ownership; never steal a demonstrably live lock. A lock or index-write failure must not silently succeed. Store reopen detects malformed version/index/manifest data. Document the concurrency protocol, corruption response and backup/recovery limitations.

6. CLI and persistent local jobs. node bin/workspace-vault.js --store PATH supports snapshot SOURCE [--label TEXT], list, get ID, restore ID DEST [--mirror] [--dry-run] [--journal PATH] [--conflict error|skip|overwrite], diff A B, verify [ID], export ID FILE, import FILE, prune --keep comma,separated,ids [--dry-run], and serve [--port N]. Successful finite commands write one JSON result to stdout; failures write a concise JSON error to stderr and exit nonzero. --help documents usage. SIGINT/SIGTERM settle work and close handles; no orphan workers. serve gets its bearer token from WORKSPACE_VAULT_TOKEN and allowed roots from WORKSPACE_VAULT_ROOTS (JSON string array).

await createServer({vault,host:'127.0.0.1',port:0,token,allowedRoots:[absoluteDirectories]}) returns {url,close} after listening; await close() stops accepting work and drains or safely checkpoints it. Refuse non-loopback hosts and empty tokens. GET /health returns {ok:true}. Other /api routes require Authorization: Bearer TOKEN; query tokens are not accepted. GET /api/snapshots, GET /api/jobs, GET /api/jobs/:id; POST /api/jobs with {type:'snapshot',source,label?}, {type:'restore',snapshotId,destination,mirror?,journalPath?}, {type:'verify',snapshotId?}, or {type:'prune',keep} returns HTTP202 {id,status}. POST /api/jobs/:id/cancel requests cancellation. Only source/destination/journal paths inside allowedRoots may be used, resolve aliases before admission, and never let a job redirect outside those roots. Wrong auth is401, malformed input400, missing ids404, conflicting Idempotency-Key reuse409. The same nonempty Idempotency-Key with equivalent JSON replays the same job; a changed body must not enqueue. Jobs are durable with ordered integer-sequence events and statuses queued,running,completed,failed,cancelled. A reopened server loads history and safely resumes/checkpoints unfinished work. GET /api/jobs/:id/events?after=N streams SSE id:<sequence> and JSON data events, replaying only sequences>N, in order; terminate the stream once a terminal job's replay is complete. Apply a documented bounded queue and concurrency=1. Cancellation must not turn a completed job into cancelled. Reject permissive cross-origin API access, malformed bodies and oversized input; user-facing errors must preserve an actionable code/message.

7. Offline dashboard. Serve an HTML/CSS/JavaScript application at /. It must work without external assets/network libraries, accept a bearer token in memory, list snapshots and jobs, submit snapshot/restore/verify jobs, show progress/error states and cancel running jobs. Use accessible labeled controls, keyboard operation, clear destructive-action confirmation, and text-safe rendering of arbitrary path/label/error strings. Include real automated browser tests or a reproducible browser verification script, and capture proof of successful/failed job transitions. A screenshot alone is insufficient. The dashboard must use the same HTTP contract and respect auth failures and disconnects.

8. Release validation. Add a maintained test suite under contrib/workspace-vault/test covering the complete API, process concurrency, corrupted imports, cancellation/listener cleanup, durable kill/restart/resume, server restart/idempotency/SSE and browser flows. Add README.md, DESIGN.md documenting formats and invariants, CHANGELOG.md, and an offline examples/backup-and-recover.js that demonstrates snapshot, dry-run, interruption/recovery and portable import using owned temporary directories with cleanup. Run all original fs-extra regression/ESM/lint checks plus your new tests, the example and real concurrent-process checks. Package into an exclusive temporary directory and verify CommonJS, ESM and CLI consumption from another directory with an empty runtime dependency set. Record actual commands, outputs, coverage gaps and limitations in VALIDATION.md. Review failure paths after the happy path passes; repair defects and rerun affected checks before final delivery. Do not weaken tests or silently skip required subsystems. No publishing, committing or network service exposure is requested.
